title: 第13章 潮声第14章 边境的灰烬
slug: 黯潮纪元异世界的崛起
content_zh:
加雷斯没多问，指了指角落的武器架：“挑一把，先看看你的底。”
陈默扫过一排长剑——标准的骑士制式剑，铁质护手，皮绳缠绕的握柄，剑刃保养得不错。他拿起第三把，掂了掂重量。比他想象中轻，但重心靠前，劈砍时惯性够大。
“用剑的？”加雷斯抱臂站着，疤痕在晨光里泛白。
“会一点。”
“会一点可不够。”加雷斯朝操场中央努嘴，“看见那根木桩了吗？三剑，让我看看你的架势。”
陈默走过去。木桩是橡木的，表面布满刀痕，有些已经深及内部。他站定，握剑，深吸一口气。
第一剑——斜劈。
剑刃切入木桩两指深，木屑飞溅。
第二剑——横斩。
同一道切口，更深了三分，剑刃卡在木纤维里。
第三剑——刺。
他拔剑，双手推剑尖，直刺切口正中央。剑尖没入四指深，震得虎口发麻。
加雷斯走过来，看了眼切口，没说话。他伸手握住剑柄，用力一拔，剑刃从木桩中脱出。他把剑翻过来，仔细看了看剑刃——没有卷口，没有崩刃。
“练过。”加雷斯说，语气里听不出是陈述还是疑问。
“三年。”陈默没撒谎。在现代，他练过三年双手剑术，不过是复原古代兵器的那种，和实战差得远。
“三年能劈出这种切口？”加雷斯把剑扔回给他，“你手上有茧，但不是剑茧。你练过别的什么？”
陈默愣了一下。他低头看自己的手——右手的茧在食指和中指根部，那是常年握毛笔和考古工具留下的。而左手掌心光滑，没有剑士该有的摩擦痕迹。
“考古。”他说，“我以前是考古学家。”
加雷斯盯着他看了三秒，然后笑了一声。那笑声很短，像是从喉咙里挤出来的：“考古学家。一个考古学家，圣光爆发，被编入骑士小队。有意思。”
他转身朝操场中央走去，声音从背后传来：“今天先热身。绕着操场跑二十圈，然后去仓库领装备。科尔曼副团长下午要见你。”

操场是标准尺寸，一圈大概四百米。二十圈，八公里。
陈默没废话，开始跑。
***
操场边缘的土路被踩得结实，每一步都能感受到地面的硬度。晨风从城墙方向吹来，夹着泥土和铁锈的气味——那是城墙上血迹干涸后留下的味道。黯潮的痕迹还没完全清理干净。
跑到第五圈，陈默注意到操场另一侧有人在练箭。十个人，站成一排，拉弓，放箭。箭矢钉在五十步外的靶子上，发出沉闷的“笃笃”声。
第七圈时，他看见了艾莉西亚。
她站在靶场边缘，穿着训练用的皮甲，手里拿着一把长弓。她拉弓的动作很流畅，从箭袋抽箭到放箭，一气呵成。箭矢正中靶心，把上一支箭劈成两半。
陈默放慢脚步，想打个招呼。
艾莉西亚转过头，看见是他，脸上没有表情。她放下弓，朝他走过来。
“你被编入第三小队了？”她问。
“嗯。加雷斯教官带的我。”
艾莉西亚沉默了几秒，目光在他脸上停留：“你昨晚的事，我听说了。引导圣光成功，稳定了失控的魔力。”
陈默等着她说下去。
“教廷的人今天会到。”艾莉西亚压低声音，“他们对你很感兴趣。小心点。”
“教廷？”
content_en:
Gareth didn't ask any further questions and pointed to the weapon rack in the corner: "Pick one, let's take a look at your bottom first."
Chen Mo glanced at a row of long swords - standard knight swords, with iron handguards, leather rope-wrapped handles, and well-maintained blades. He picked up the third one and weighed it. It was lighter than he expected, but its center of gravity was forward, and it had enough inertia when chopping.
"With a sword?" Gareth stood with his arms folded, his scars whitening in the morning light.
"Know a little."
"A little knowledge is not enough." Gareth pouted toward the center of the playground, "Did you see that wooden stake? Sanjian, let me see your posture."
Chen Mo walked over. The wooden pile was made of oak, and its surface was covered with knife marks, some of which had penetrated deep into the interior. He stood still, held his sword, and took a deep breath.
The first sword - diagonal slash.
The sword blade cut into the wooden stake two fingers deep, and sawdust flew away.
The second sword - horizontal slash.
The same cut was made three points deeper, and the sword blade was stuck in the wood fiber.
The third sword - stabbing.
He drew his sword, pushed the tip of the sword with both hands, and stabbed straight into the center of the incision. The tip of the sword penetrated four fingers deep, causing the tiger's mouth to feel numb.
Gareth came over, looked at the incision, and said nothing. He reached out and grasped the hilt of the sword, pulled it out hard, and the blade came out of the wooden stake. He turned the sword over and looked at the blade carefully - there was no curling or chipping.
"Practice," Gareth said, unable to tell whether it was a statement or a question.
"Three years." Chen Mo didn't lie. In modern times, he practiced two-handed swordsmanship for three years, but it was just a kind of restoration of ancient weapons, which was far from actual combat.
"You can make such an incision in three years?" Gareth threw the sword back to him. "You have calluses on your hands, but they are not sword calluses. What else have you practiced?"
Chen Mo was stunned for a moment. He looked down at his hands - the calluses on his right hand were at the base of his index and middle fingers, which were left from holding brushes and archaeological tools all the time. The palm of the left hand is smooth, with no traces of friction that a swordsman should have.
"Archaeology," he said, "I used to be an archaeologist."
Gareth stared at him for three seconds, then laughed. The laughter was short, as if squeezed from the throat: "Archaeologist. An archaeologist, the Holy Light broke out, and was incorporated into the knight squad. Interesting."
He turned around and walked towards the center of the playground, and a voice came from behind: "Today, let's warm up first. Run twenty laps around the playground, and then go to the warehouse to get equipment. Deputy Commander Coleman wants to see you in the afternoon."
The playground is of standard size, with a circle of about 400 meters. Twenty laps, eight kilometers.
Chen Mo didn't talk nonsense and started running.
***
The dirt road at the edge of the playground is well-trodden, and you can feel the hardness of the ground with every step you take. The morning breeze blew from the direction of the city wall, carrying the smell of earth and rust - the smell left after the blood on the city wall dried. The traces of the dark tide have not yet been completely cleared away.
On the fifth lap, Chen Mo noticed someone practicing archery on the other side of the playground. Ten people stood in a row, drawing their bows and shooting arrows. The arrow hit the target fifty steps away, making a dull "click" sound.
On the seventh lap, he saw Alicia.
She stood at the edge of the range, wearing training leather armor and holding a longbow. Her bow-drawing movements were smooth, from drawing the arrow in the quiver to releasing the arrow, all in one go. The arrow hit the bullseye, splitting the previous arrow in half.
Chen Mo slowed down and wanted to say hello.
Alicia turned her head and saw it was him, her face expressionless. She lowered her bow and walked towards him.
"Have you been assigned to the third team?" she asked.
"Yes. Instructor Gareth led me."
Alicia was silent for a few seconds, her eyes lingering on his face: "I heard about what happened to you last night. You successfully guided the Holy Light and stabilized the out-of-control magic power."
Chen Mo waited for her to continue.
"People from the Holy See will arrive today." Alicia lowered her voice, "They are very interested in you. Be careful."
"The Holy See?"
